macro.headline: Choppy indices, energy leadership, oil-driven risk premium building
macro.story:
The tape is mixed but not broken. SPY closed at $748.28, up 0.83% on the day but down 0.47% over five sessions, sitting above both its 50- and 200-day moving averages with RSI at 52.75 — neutral momentum. QQQ is softer: below its 50-day, RSI 48.11, down 4.17% over 21 days, with the histogram deeply negative (-2.54). VIX printed 17.61, up 12.4% in five days, and VIX3M sits at 20.54 (contango preserved). The Dow and Russell are firmer than the Nasdaq, a rotation footprint. On commodities, WTI crude is up 9.35% in five days and 16.33% in 21 to $87.04 (RSI 64.95), copper is stretched (RSI 62 in overbought-extended Bollinger territory), gold and silver are still in downtrends despite this week's bounces, and the 10-year yield is at 4.63% and rising. DXY holds above its 50- and 200-day.

The tracked conversation is genuinely split, and the substance tells the story better than any tally. On one side, sentiment is flagging escalating US–Iran rhetoric — with chart reads showing Brent breaking $94 and WTI reclaiming $85 — as the immediate driver of the oil bid and the VIX creep; the Strait of Hormuz language and 'bomb-a-bridge-per-shot' posture are being treated as a live geopolitical premium, not noise. On the other side, the dominant view leans firmly bearish on beta and large-cap tech into this backdrop, pointing to AMD, SMCI, SPY and GOOGL as vulnerable, with a widely-shared chart read arguing S&P 500 earnings contribution is quietly rotating from hyperscalers (36% → 9%) to semis (16% → 48%) by Q2 2026 — a composition shift that pressures the mega-cap concentration trade. A quieter bullish stream is hunting individual setups (TXO, SBET, NBIS, MU, SNDK) and calling out 'an insane amount of stocks setting up.' This is consistent with what the sector data shows: leadership has moved out of Technology and into Energy, Financials, Healthcare and Real Estate.

Under the surface, the rotation is unambiguous. Energy is the only HOT sector (score 9.8, RSI 65), and Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing carries the highest rotation score in the radar (~97th percentile RS rank, 3 months into a hot spell, roughly halfway through a typical run, up 5.4% since the signal fired). Real Estate, Healthcare, Financials and Staples all qualify. Technology (score 2.8), Nasdaq 100, Materials and Consumer Discretionary sit at the bottom — the last two are below their 50-day. This is a defensive-plus-energy tape wearing a bull-regime jersey (SPY drawdown only -2.3%).

Forward watch: whether crude holds above $85 and the 10-year yield keeps grinding higher (the yield curve just re-steepened +60% in 21 days off a low base). If oil breaks and the geopolitical premium unwinds, the leadership handoff to energy could reverse quickly; if VIX pushes through 20, macro confidence steps down. For now: bull regime, neutral index momentum, live rotation into energy and defensives, and a sentiment split that mirrors the price action rather than fighting it.
